Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Consumer Brands Inc., or GCB, Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for queuing questions will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss GCB's Q3 2024 results. With me on the call are Jane Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Patel, Chief Financial Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Marketing Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jane Thompson.

Jane Thompson:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. GCB delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

Our discussion today will cover four key aspects: first, geographic performance across developed and emerging markets; second, supply chain efficiencies and productivity savings; third, A&P spend and ROI; and fourth, marketing campaign effectiveness.

I will now turn the call over to Mike Patel to provide more detail on our financial results.

Mike Patel:
Thank you, Jane. As Jane mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $4.6 billion, representing a 6% increase compared to the prior year as reported, or 5% on an organic basis excluding FX and acquisitions. Gross margin expanded to 48.2%, driven by supply chain efficiencies, pricing actions, and lower input costs following last year's spikes in commodities like cocoa and palm oil. Operating income reached $985 million, up 8% year-over-year. Diluted earnings per share were $1.28. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.

Let me expand on these results, starting with our geographic performance, which highlights the resilience of our CPG franchises in a challenging macro backdrop. Our portfolio showed strength across both developed and emerging markets. Developed markets, making up 65% of sales, achieved 2% organic growth, while emerging markets—at 35% of the mix—powered ahead with 12% organic growth, more than compensating for softer volumes in mature areas.

In developed markets, North America, our biggest region at 40% of group revenues, grew 3% organically. This was spearheaded by our leading snacks and beverages, where power brands like ZestCrunch chips and PureThirst energy drinks picked up 1.2 points of market share according to IRI data. Premiumization played a big role, with protein-enriched options and zero-sugar variants appealing to health-focused Gen Z shoppers. E-commerce now accounts for 18% of North American sales, up from 14% last year, boosted by our Shopify direct-to-consumer site and tie-ups with Amazon and Walmart+. Still, inflation-fatigued consumers limited volume gains to 0.5%, as some shifted to private labels in categories like household cleaners.

Europe, 25% of revenues, was flat organically on a constant-currency basis, hit by lingering energy costs and regulations. The UK and Germany posted mid-single-digit drops in laundry and personal care, where EcoWash detergents competed fiercely against Unilever's Persil and P&G's Ariel. Positively, our sustainability push—100% recyclable packaging for GlowEssence skincare—lifted market share by 0.8 points per Nielsen in Western Europe. Margins stayed at 22%, thanks to 4% average pricing and efficiencies from consolidating European distribution centers.

Emerging markets were the standout growth driver at 12% organic, with volumes up 8% versus 5-7% category averages. Asia-Pacific, 15% of sales, jumped 15% organically, led by India and Southeast Asia. India's urbanization and rising middle class fueled our foods business, as SpiceBurst ready-meals grabbed 2.5 share points in the $15 billion organized retail space, much like Nestlé's Maggi. China delivered high-teens growth in beverages, with e-commerce via Tmall and JD.com hitting 25% of sales, up from 18%, including new low-sugar options for the post-COVID wellness trend.

Latin America, 12% of revenues, advanced 10% organically amid FX swings in Brazil and Argentina. Mexico shone at +14%, where VivaFresh deodorants benefited from higher incomes and distribution into over 5,000 tienditas through our micro-depot system, echoing PepsiCo's approach. Volumes rose 7%, with 1.5 share points gained in snacks per Kantar Worldpanel.

Africa and the Middle East, 8% of sales, grew 8% organically. Nigeria and South Africa gained from out-of-home activations, increasing impulse beverage buys by 12% via coolers in 50,000+ outlets. Affordability packs—smaller SKUs at 20-30% lower prices—expanded reach in low-income areas, similar to Coca-Cola's emerging market tactics.

On the P&L, developed markets posted 21.5% core operating margins from premium scale and easing input costs. Emerging margins widened 150 basis points to 18.2%, aided by local sourcing—like our Vietnam rice-snack facility cutting logistics 10%—and firm pricing amid 8-10% inflation.

Looking ahead strategically, we're committing $500 million in capex over 18 months: 40% for India and Indonesia capacity, 30% for AI demand forecasting via SAP S/4HANA, and the rest for D2C on Shopee and Mercado Libre. In developed markets, R&D is up 10% year-over-year for plant-based innovations and ESG to counter disruptors like Olipop. We see developed markets accelerating to 3-4% organic growth in the second half on easing inflation and holidays, with emerging at 10-12% via premiumization and channels—aiming for emerging at 40% of sales by FY2026.

Shifting to supply chain efficiencies and productivity savings, these were a major tailwind, offsetting a $285 million headwind and expanding gross margin by a full point to 48.2%, adding about 170 basis points to adjusted EBITDA margin at 22.4% for the year to date, up 120 basis points year-over-year.

This builds on our 2021 Supply Chain Resilience Program. Amid 15-20% raw material inflation in edible oils, PET resins, and pulp, these savings protected margins on key brands like FreshGlow laundry detergents, NutriVital snack bars, and PureEssence personal care, which drive 65% of our $18.2 billion annual top line.

Full-year productivity savings hit $285 million, up 22% from $233 million in 2022, with supply chain costs at 19.1% of sales, a 4.8% improvement beating P&G and Unilever's 3-4%. Inventory turns rose from 8.7x to 10.2x, freeing $420 million in working capital—15 fewer DIO days—to support a 12% dividend increase and $1.2 billion in buybacks.

Regionally, North America (55% of revenue) generated $140 million, leveraging 12 automated DCs with AS/RS and AGVs for 12% lower fulfillment costs and 99.8% pick accuracy, countering 8% ocean freight hikes.

Europe yielded $85 million via 6% manufacturing yield from Zero Waste to Landfill across six plants. We secured 70% RSPO-certified palm oil at 10-15% better prices, cut Scope 3 emissions 25%, and nearshored 20% to Eastern Europe, trimming lead times 18 days despite deforestation rules.

Emerging markets (30% of sales) delivered $60 million despite Brazil soy swings and India monsoons, localizing 40% more SKUs to cut duties and FX risk. APAC slashed logistics 15% via Alibaba Cloud and JD Logistics, reducing urban delivery 22% in Shanghai and Mumbai.

Core enablers include a $450 million three-year digital push: SAP S/4HANA at 85% coverage and Blue Yonder AI cutting forecast error 28%, stockouts to 1.2%. Digital twins at Ohio and Guadalajara plants lifted OEE to 89%, adding 7% throughput sans capex.

Procurement's Value Engineering redesigned 1,200 formulations—like bio-based swaps in FreshGlow—saving $95 million. Our GCB Carrier Network cut carriers to 12, miles 18%, fuel surcharges 11% via FourKites. Regenerative ag pilots with 500 Midwest farmers trimmed corn syrup fertilizer 14%.

Under Agile Supply Chain 2025, we target $350 million more next year for 200 bps EBITDA gains: dual-sourcing 90% top ingredients, three new micro-fulfillment centers in Mexico City and Hyderabad, IBM Food Trust blockchain. With 15% cost edge, we handle 20% input spikes, protecting margins while upping A&P 250 bps.

Now, on A&P spend and ROI, we invested $1.2 billion in Q3, up 4% year-over-year constant currency, or 18% of net sales. This zero-based approach prioritizes incrementality amid inflation and soft staples growth.

Consumer advertising ($650 million, 54% of A&P, +7%) spanned TV, CTV, digital, social. Trade spend ($550 million, flat) focused shopper marketing, slotting, retailer media like Walmart Connect—retail media up 25% to $180 million at 20-30% lower CPMs.

Blended ROMI rose to 3.8x from 3.4x, via MMM, Google's Meridian, Nielsen causal. Digital ROAS hit 5.2x, e.g., FreshGlow skincare's TikTok influencers drove 15% lift at 4.5x. TV for PowerCrunch bars yielded 2.8x, shifting GRPs to CTV for 25% efficiency.

Digital is 42% of consumer ad (up from 35%), via Salesforce/Adobe CDP, Epsilon AI lookalikes, 18% programmatic CPM gains. Shopper marketing cut waste 12% with accrual terms; trade NPS at 72.

North America (55% A&P) hit 4.2x ROMI via Amazon DSP (PureFlow +22% NMV), DTC subs at 8%. EMEA at 3.1x leaned local value packs amid contraction. APAC 4.5x with Tmall/Douyin, JioMart +28% ACV.

Q4 A&P at 17-18% of sales, $200 million to AR try-ons, gen-AI like Jasper for 20% faster creative, loyalty for 15% FY25 ROMI lift—fueling 2.2% organic growth, 50 bps share vs. Unilever/Colgate.

Finally, marketing campaign effectiveness drove 4.2x ROMI portfolio-wide, up 14% from 3.7x, on $1.2 billion budget +8% sequentially amid softer media costs.

Digital (42%, up from 35%) via CTV, Amazon DSP, Walmart Connect, TikTok—generated 58% sales lift. Traditional (30%) at 2.8x for FreshBurst sodas, Everyday Essentials.

The 'Refresh the Everyday' FreshBurst summer campaign across 15 markets featured TikTok UGC (250M impressions, 12M views), CTV on Hulu/Roku (85M households)—+22% NA velocity, $180M revenue, 5.1x ROMI, AOV +11% to $28.50 via bundles. Attribution via Meridian, GCB Rewards app.

North America (45% sales) at 4.5x, CAC down 28% to $4.20, +1.2 bev share vs. Keurig Dr Pepper. EMEA 3.9x on 'PurePlanet' EcoGlow sustainability, +16% UK/Germany sales. APAC 4.8x (+20% YoY) via WeChat GlowBeauty (+35% e-comm, +42% repeats). LatAm 3.6x shifted to micro-influencers (+3x engagement), +8 pts Brazil share.

Tech: Trade Desk DCO +27% CTR, +19% conversions; Snowflake/Segment CDP (2.5B signals), 92% attribution, -$45M waste. LiveRamp pilots for cookieless.

'Performance Always-On' stresses geo-holdouts (67% lift), CLV +12% to $245, 65% omnichannel. Q4 4.5x ROMI, $350M holiday incl. Snapchat AR, Alexa pilots—outpacing 2-3% category.

These elements position us strongly for the year ahead, with organic growth of 4-5% and EPS expansion in the mid-teens.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for submitting questions will be repeated. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on consumer spending habits, particularly in developed versus emerging markets?

Jane Thompson:
Thanks, John. Inflation continues to pressure households, but our geographic split shows resilience. In developed markets like North America and Europe, consumers are value-seeking, trading down in staples, which capped our volumes at low-single digits. However, premium power brands like ZestCrunch and GlowEssence held share through health and sustainability appeals. Emerging markets tell a different story—stronger middle-class growth in India, Mexico, and China drove volume expansion, with affordability packs and localized innovations offsetting local inflation. Overall, our pricing discipline and efficiencies let us invest behind brands without sacrificing margins.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan.

Emily Chen:
Regarding your new product FreshGlow skincare line, what are the projections for its market impact?

Sarah Chen:
Great question, Emily. FreshGlow has been a breakout since launch, leveraging TikTok Shop and nano-influencer campaigns for Gen Z. Early data shows 15% sales lift at 4.5x ROAS, with e-commerce driving 25% of category sales in key markets. Projections: we expect 1-2 share points in North America and EMEA by year-end, expanding to APAC with AR try-ons. Sustainability packaging aligns with ESG trends, positioning it for 20%+ growth in FY25 as premium skincare outpaces the category.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley.

David Lee:
Can you provide more details on the promotional spending for the quarter?

Mike Patel:
Sure, David. Promo was embedded in our $550 million trade spend, flat year-over-year but optimized for ROI. We focused accrual-based terms on high-velocity SKUs, cutting pay-to-stay waste 12%, with retail media up 25% for better CPMs. This contributed to 3.8x blended ROMI, especially in shopper marketing via Walmart Connect and Kroger. In emerging markets, it supported velocity gains; in developed, it defended share against private labels. Q4 holds steady at 17-18% of sales, funding holiday pushes.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Jane Thompson for closing remarks.

Jane Thompson:
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your questions and participation in today's call. We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders, with balanced growth from our global footprint, efficient operations, and high-ROI marketing. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the GCB Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
